newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADIAN DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER AFTER U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER AFTER U.S. DATA.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended firmer on Wednesday around C$1.3921
(US$0.7183) from earlier lows around C$1.3940 (US$0.7173) and
Tuesday's close at C$1.3934 (US$0.7176) * Canada unit seen
overnight * Low U.S. producer prices sparked modest rally in
Canadian currency, offset by selling later in session
The U.S. Commerce Department also reported this morning that U.S. retail sales rose 0.6 percent in July, below expectations of a 0.7 percent rise.
Analysts said the data eased pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates, prompting some selling of the U.S. currency and some buying of Canadian dollars.

Traders said they expected the currency to trade between C$1.3915 and C$1.3945 overnight. "It seems the last couple of days the Far East sells Canada and then London turns around and buys Canada. Will the pattern repeat itself? There's a decent chance it will," another trader said.
